name: Health data (HealthKit and Health Connect)
plain: Reads and writes health records such as steps, heart rate and sleep, one data type at a time.
meaning: Sleep, heart rate and cycle data show conditions and habits. Both OSes grant per data type.

android.permission: android.permission.health.READ_* and WRITE_* per data type; READ_HEALTH_DATA_IN_BACKGROUND; READ_HEALTH_DATA_HISTORY
android.prompt_ui: Health Connect permission sheet with per type toggles
android.persistence: Until revoked; permission usage visible in Health Connect
android.store_policy: Play: Health apps declaration; health data not for ads
android.note: Reads default to 30 days before first grant; older data needs READ_HEALTH_DATA_HISTORY

ios.prompt_ui: Health access sheet with per type toggles
ios.store_policy: App Review 5.1.3: no use for advertising or storing in iCloud
ios.note: Apps cannot tell if read access was denied; denial looks like no data

limits.headline: Can see and add health data such as steps and sleep, one type at a time
limits.user_action: You tap Connect health data and switch on the types you want to share
can: See the data types you allow, such as steps, heart rate and sleep
Add new records for the types you allow
Use background access on Android with a separate permission
Check older history on Android with the history permission
cannot: See types you left off in the sheet
See more than the last 30 days on Android before first grant, without the history permission
Tell on iPhone if you denied; it looks like no data
Keep access after you turn the switches off
limits.reach_label: Only the data types you allow
limits.differs: Android Health Connect limits old data to 30 days unless you allow history. iPhone HealthKit hides a denial.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app read and write health records such as steps, heart rate and sleep.

marketing.name: HealthKit
marketing.pitch: Developer pitch: a central place for health data, with people in control of what each app can see and write.

story.for_you: A screen lists each kind of data an app wants, like steps, sleep or heart rate. You turn on only the ones you like, and you can change it later in the Health app.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to read your history, write new workouts and connect with watches and other apps. It saves them from building their own sensors and gives users clear controls.

use_cases.example: A workout app reads your steps and writes a new run so the Health app has it.
A sleep app reads your nights and shows trends.
A period tracking app writes cycle data and reads symptoms.
A watch app shares heart rate and activity with the phone.
A game gives rewards for steps you walked.
A diabetes app reads glucose from a sensor.
Apple bans using HealthKit data for ads or selling it.

story.android_note: Android uses Health Connect with its own list of per data permissions.
story.ios_note: Granted per data type, with a bundled read and write choice in a single sheet.

technical_bounds: Read denial is hidden on iOS
Health Connect history window limited by default

history.change: Health Connect built into the platform
